items.title: Jussi Erosen kolumni: Somen haittoja lapsille ja nuorille on ehkäisty väärässä päässä ongelmaa
items.summary: Ympäri maailmaa ollaan huolissaan sosiaalisen median vaikutuksista alaikäisiin. Some-alustojen säännöt kieltävät jo nykyisellään niiden käytön nuorimmilta, mutta tämä ei tunnetusti estä mitään käytännössä. Älypuhelimet tarjoavat kyllä keinoja erilaisten käyttörajoitusten luomiseen lapsille ja nuorille, mutta monet vanhemmat eivät tunne niitä tai kokevat käytön hankalaksi. Kun vapaaehtoinen kontrolli ei toimi, lainsäätäjien katseet ovat kääntyneet pakon suuntaan. Useissa maissa on säädetty lakeja pakollisesta iän tarkastamisesta sosiaalisen median käyttäjiltä.

items.title: ARTEX and Friends: Enter Agentic Offensive Frameworks
items.summary: Recent intrusions in which threat actors have been observed weaponizing agentic frameworks to execute highly-automated intrusions has put a spotlight on evolving adversarial use of LLMs. In our September 2026 report, Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) noted that forward leaning adversaries were beginning to transition from basic prompting to agentic workflows and LLM-enabled automation. Since this publication, GTIG and Mandiant have observed multiple threat actors abusing the open-source, agentic pentesting frameworks ARTEX, Hexstrike and CAIRN in incident response engagements to conduct a broad range of actions across multiple phases of the attack life cycle. This activity has been seen across the threat landscape, as noted in a recent Wiz report. The emergence of Artex and similar agentic offensive intrusion frameworks underscores a broader shift toward threat actor adoption of open source multi-agent offensive frameworks, as well as potentially custom agentic harnesses. This represents a paradigm shift towards intrusions occurring at machine speed, with the automated chaining of complex attack paths scaling intrusions exponentially. While the mechanics of the intrusions remain the same, such as using compromised credentials and targeting unpatched systems, the speed and scale at which frameworks can exploit these known weaknesses introduces a new defensive challenge. Security teams, developers, and system administrators will need to fundamentally rethink defense strategies to counter scalable, autonomous software. We also provide defensive strategies from Mandiant Consulting. The defensive strategies suggested—control-plane isolation, short-lived credentials, least privilege, segmentation, and behavioral detection—are long-standing security best practices.

items.title: NetamLoader Malware Targets Government Windows 10 Systems in Asia via .NET Injection
items.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of what has been described as a "highly sophisticated infection chain" targeting government organizations in Asia. The activity, detailed by Kaspersky this week, targeted a custom Windows 10 build used exclusively by government entities in Asia and involves the deployment of a previously undocumented .NET assembly-loading framework codenamed NetamLoader. The attack has not been attributed to any known threat actor or group. Nor is it clear if the intrusion compromised more than one system and allowed the hackers to steal any sensitive information. The Russian cybersecurity company said the artifact was detected in the first half of 2026, packaged inside a Windows cabinet archive (CAB) file placed in a directory that stores Windows operating system update packages.

items.title: Alpine Linux rebuilds GitLab after attempted RCE attack
items.summary: Hackers attempted to exploit a critical GitLab vulnerability in Alpine Linux's development infrastructure on October 20–21, prompting the open-source project to rebuild its GitLab server and reset all passwords over concerns of a possible compromise. The attacks targeted CVE-2026-97229, a maximum-severity remote code execution flaw, repeatedly crashing GitLab processes, with some attempts coming close to succeeding. Although Alpine Linux found no evidence that attackers executed code or tampered with its software packages and releases, it could not rule out a successful compromise due to missing logs and a lack of outbound connection records.
